title: Low-Cal Malaysian Satay Tofu
subtitle: with Creamy Coconut Cauliflower
description: Just wait till you try this moreish cauliflower puree with creamy coconut milk! Topped with satay tofu tossed in mild Malaysian spices, it makes a low-cal meal that's both delicious and satisfying.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Coarsely chop the cauliflower stem, then cut the head into small florets. Thinly slice the spring onion on an angle. Crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Halve the tofu pieces. Crumble 1 stock cube into a heatproof jug, add 125ml (½ cup) boiling water and stir to dissolve.

Cook cauliflower: Put the cauliflower, garlic, coconut milk and stock in a medium saucepan and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, for 20 mins or until the cauliflower is tender. Remove the pan from the heat.

Warm tofu: Meanwhile, heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Cook the tofu for 2 mins each side or until golden and warmed through. Remove from the pan. Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in the pan over medium-high heat. Cook the spring onion and curry powder for 1-2 mins until fragrant. Add the tofu and turn to coat. Remove the pan from the heat.
Blend cauliflower: Blend the cauliflower mixture with a stick blender or food processor (see Kitchen hack) until smooth. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.
Serve up: Divide the cauliflower puree, tofu and spring onion among bowls. Enjoy!
Kitchen hack: If you don't have a stick blender or food processor, simply mash the cauliflower with a potato masher. The result won't be as smooth, but it will be just as delicious!
